title: Nothing Crosses the Gap
logline: A block of hardwood put into dry-zone ground in a single season forty years ago comes down in a single season now, on a date decided by people who are not there to see it, and within weeks the same ground is planted again with a stand that takes nothing whatever from the one that ended.
human_question: If nothing at all goes across from the end of one thing to the beginning of the next, in what sense is it the same thing?

place.what_kind_of_place: A state forest plantation in the northern dry zone: rectangular blocks of one hardwood species, all of one age, laid out on lines across flat or gently rolling ground that was degraded natural forest before it was planted. The blocks are separated by fire traces and extraction roads and surrounded by scrub, tank-fed paddy and villages. Each block was established in one planting season and is managed on a rotation of roughly two decades, thinned once or twice, and then taken out entirely in one operation, under licence, by a felling crew and their machines. Beside every mature block there is usually a block already cut, a block coming up, and a block of the same age still standing, so the whole rotation is visible in one landscape at one time.
place.why_it_is_worth_watching: Because a plantation is a cohort, and a cohort makes something visible that nothing else in a landscape does. Every tree in the block is the same age, because every one of them was put in during the same few weeks; so when the end of the rotation arrives, it arrives for all of them at once, and from the air the block is a rectangle of one colour going to a rectangle of stumps in ranks over a few weeks. It is also the only landscape where the whole sequence is laid out side by side: cut ground, planting lines, a young stand, a closing stand and a stand at its end, all within one frame from height. On the ground it is quiet, orderly, technical work in very hot flat light: a mark on a trunk, a saw, a fall, a number written on a cut end. And a single stump, read from directly above, contains the whole life of the thing at the moment it has stopped.
place.what_moves_or_changes: Almost nothing, for twenty years, and then everything in one season. Within the felling season the change is daily and irreversible. The light in the block changes as the canopy goes, the ground temperature changes, the dust changes, and then the rains come and the planting goes in. Nothing here can be scheduled by a crew except the hour; the felling season is set by the rotation and the licence, and the planting is set by the rain.
place.when_it_looks_best: Two windows about two months apart: the dry-season felling, when the light is hard, the dust is up and the blocks are being taken out, and the first weeks of the rains, when the planting goes into the same ground. Within a day, the first and last hour, when low sun goes down the planting lines and the ranks of stumps throw shadows that make the geometry unmistakable from height.

two_layers.without_the_philosophy: A film about a planted forest reaching the end of the arrangement it was planted under, and about the unhurried, entirely ordinary work of ending it. Ranks of trunks, the geometry only the drone can see, a marking crew, a saw, a fall, cut ends and numbers, the ground opening to the sky, stumps in rows, the rain, the planting, the young stand a year on, and the next block along still standing and untouched. It has a complete shape with nothing said over it, and anyone who likes landscape, geometry or watching skilled people work has a whole piece here.
two_layers.with_the_philosophy: The same season becomes the sources' account of the end of a life, which is far more ordinary and far stranger than most people expect. Dying, in these texts, is not an event of a different kind: it is the same run of mind-moments through the same doors that has been going on all along, only shorter, because the physical base of mind is weak by then. And at the last moment there is no interval and no traveller: the final moment of one existence is followed immediately by the first of the next, and nothing mental or physical goes across. A cohort that ends on a date set decades ago, on ground that is planted again within weeks, is the shape of that claim. The voice says outright that the sources are describing minds and that a plantation has none.

sequence.on_screen: First light, high and looking straight down. Dry scrub, a tank in the distance, and set into it rectangles: one of dark even canopy with ranks showing through it, one of pale stumps in rows, one of low green lines, one of bare red ground.
sequence.voice: Every tree in that dark block went into the ground in the same few weeks, more than forty years ago. Because of that, they will all come out in the same few weeks, this year. The date was not decided by anybody who is here.

sequence.on_screen: Ground level in the standing block: a crew walking the lines, a mark painted low on a trunk, the saw carried in, the cut, the fall, the branches taken off, a number written on the cut end. Done without ceremony and without hurry.
sequence.voice: The texts are unexpectedly plain about dying. It is not a different kind of event. It is the same process of noticing that has been running the whole time, at one of the five senses or at the mind, with the same steps in the same order [C062-M:L3]. The only difference they name is that it is shorter, because the physical base of mind is weak by then: five active moments instead of the usual seven [C062-P:L25; C062-P:L27]. They are talking about minds, and this block has none. What it can show is the shape.

sequence.on_screen: The last standing tree in a block, alone in a field of stumps, filmed from a distance in flat light. Then the same work done to it as to the first.
sequence.voice: And the moment that ends it, the texts say, is of the same kind as the quiet background flow that has been running under the whole life whenever nothing much was happening [C062-M:L43]. The end is not made of different material from the middle.

sequence.on_screen: Directly above a single stump: the rings out from the centre to the bark, wide years and narrow years. Then back at height: the whole block as stumps in ranks.
sequence.voice: Which of a life's actions decides what comes next, the books answer with a queue and not a scale: gravest first, then whatever is done or recalled near the end, then whatever was done over and over, then anything left [C056-P:L117]. Their own picture for why a queue is not a scale is a cattle pen: the worn-out old cow put in last has to lie by the gate and goes out before all of them in the morning [C056-P:L119]. It is the same here. Which of these came down first was decided by the road and the reach of the machine. Nothing about it says which tree was best.

sequence.on_screen: The first rains. The same ground, wet, steaming, with the stumps in it. A planting line being opened, seedlings going in between the stumps of the old rows.
sequence.voice: Here is the part people find hardest. Both sources say that the last moment of one existence is followed by the first moment of the next with no interval at all, and that nothing mental and nothing physical goes across between them [C061-P:L75; C061-P:L85; C061-M:L15]. Not a memory, not a particle. What begins is genuinely new. It begins only because of what ended.

sequence.on_screen: A year on. The same rectangle, now low green lines with the grey stumps still standing among them. A sign at the road with a number and a year on it.
sequence.voice: And yet the sign says it is the same plantation, and the people working it talk about it that way. The Margaya allows that manner of speaking, and is exact about why: the gap is no longer than the gap between one moment of mind and the next, and because the stream is unbroken you may speak of the one who ended and the one who begins as one, not because anything travelled [C061-M:L17]. That is what continuity without a traveller sounds like when somebody says it out loud.

sequence.on_screen: Last light at height. The young block, the cut block, and beyond them the next mature block still standing, untouched, with maybe twenty years left on it. No commentary over the final minute.
sequence.voice: Two refusals before we leave. The Pradeepika says the thing that comes up at the end is put there by the action that is ready to ripen, and is not brought by parents, relatives, teachers or gods [C061-P:L29], so nothing in these texts licenses the idea that a good last minute can be arranged by anybody standing nearby. And nothing in them says that a calm end or a hard one shows what a person was, or where anything went. The sequence runs on from one existence into the next until it stops, and the texts describe only one way it stops, which is not by anybody's arrangement [C062-M:L45–L47; C062-P:L198–L200].

concept_merge.why_together: C062 gives the shape of an ending and C061 gives the thing that is not there at the join, and a plantation rotation is the only landscape that holds both without a person in it. C062 holds that dying is an ordinary near-death cognitive process running at any of the five sense doors or at the mind door [C062-M:L3], that it is shortened to five impulsion moments because the physical base of mind is weak [C062-P:L25; C062-P:L27], that the death-moment consciousness is of the same type as the life-continuum that has been running all along [C062-M:L43], and that the stream runs on from existence to existence until it ends, with the one exception the texts describe [C062-M:L45–L47; C062-P:L198–L200]. C061 holds that the last moment is followed by the first moment of a new existence with no interval [C061-P:L75], that nothing mental or physical passes over [C061-P:L85; C061-M:L15], that the licence to speak of one being is granted by the continuity of the stream and not by any traveller [C061-M:L17], and that what surfaces at the end is presented by the ripening deed and not placed there by relatives, teachers or gods [C061-P:L29]. C056 is here for one beat, because a felling block raises the question of order on its own and the sources have an exact answer to it, including their own pen-and-gate picture for why order is not weight [C056-P:L117; C056-P:L119]. An even-aged cohort ending on a date set before anyone present was involved, with new planting in the same ground weeks later, gives all of that as geometry.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That continuity needs no traveller, and that this is observable rather than mystical once you find something whose beginning and end are both dated and neither of which shares any material with the other. C062 alone is an analysis of moments nobody can watch. C061 alone is a denial with nothing to deny it about. C056 alone is a list. Together, on ground that is planted twice in one lifetime, they let a viewer look at the join. The old version of this idea got the same three concepts by following a monk into houses where people were dying. This one gets them from a plantation, which cannot be asked to consent, cannot be bereaved, and does not have a family in the next room.

concept_links.why: The digest's account of dying as an ordinary cognitive process is the film's spine, and it is the reason the film can exist without a dying person. The near-death process runs at any of the five sense doors or at the mind door, with the deed itself available only at the mind door [C062-M:L3]; it is shortened to five impulsion moments, always of the sense-sphere kind, because the heart-base is weak at that time [C062-P:L25; C062-P:L27]; the death-moment consciousness is of the same type as the life-continuum [C062-M:L43]; and the continuum runs from rebirth-linking to death-moment and on into the next existence until it stops, with the arahant's final process taking impermanence as its object so that nothing follows [C062-M:L45–L47; C062-P:L198–L200]. Every limit in the digest that bears on this film is kept, and two are spoken on screen. The film never says a last thought decides anything, because the digest is explicit that the kind of dying mind is tied to what was built up over a life and not to a single thought anyone can plan. It never reads a manner of dying as a verdict, and it says so out loud, which is also why it contains no dying person, no patient, no hospital and no family in grief. The signs of destination are not offered as near-death experience reports. The rebirth outcomes and their realms are not narrated at all, and are never applied even by implication to anybody. The claim that sensory care at a bedside secures a good rebirth is refused rather than repeated. The film's one novel risk, that a plantation might be heard as having a mind-continuum, is handled by saying plainly in the second beat that the texts are describing minds and that this block has none.

The digest's rebirth teaching proper is the film's second half and its title. Rebirth follows death with no interval, and the round continues while craving for existence is uncut [C061-P:L75]; nothing mental or physical passes over [C061-P:L85; C061-M:L15]; the gap is no longer than between two moments of mind, and the licence to call the one who died and the one who begins a single person is granted by the unbroken stream, not by anything travelling along it [C061-M:L17]; and the object at the end is presented by the deed ready to ripen and is not brought by parents, relatives, teachers or gods [C061-P:L29]. The digest's distortions are refused, most of them explicitly. No soul moves into a new body. Nobody waits in an in-between state. Nothing here says a last thought can be arranged by the people in the room. Above all, the digest's statement that 'we live on through our legacy and in people's memories' is not the teaching is honoured structurally: the film never suggests that anything of the old stand is in the new one, and the sixth beat is built precisely to show what the sources do and do not mean by calling it the same. The digest's open question, about how 'not placed there by others' sits with the same source's list of things present at a deathbed, does not arise here, because the film contains no deathbed and narrates none of that list.

Linked for one beat, on the two lines that bear on a felling order. The sources give the sequence as weighty first, then what is done or recalled near the end, then what is habitual, then whatever is left [C056-P:L117], and their own illustration of why a sequence is not a ranking is the decrepit cow that, put into the pen last and finding no room, leaves before all the others in the morning [C056-P:L119]. Standing in a block where the order of felling is set by the extraction road, that is exactly the right thing to say and it is honest about what the order does not mean. The digest's uncertainty about the compressed syntax of the simile line is recorded in unknowns and the beat is written so that it does not depend on either reading. The digest's naming of hunting and fishing as examples of habitual occupations is not used, here or anywhere in this group. The digest's warning that no observer can see what arises in a dying mind, and that a peaceful death proves nothing, is spoken in the film's last beat. The traditional narratives, the weighty-kamma rankings and the heinous acts are not narrated.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: That in this analysis the end of something is made of the same stuff as the middle of it, only shorter; that what follows an ending begins immediately and takes nothing across; and that calling the two the same is a way of speaking about an unbroken chain of causes rather than a claim that something survived. And that none of this gives anybody a technique for managing an ending, or a way of reading one from the outside.
what_must_be_real: A licensed, ordinary felling and replanting on its own schedule, filmed with the agreement of the forest authority and the crew. Nothing is felled, marked, moved, stacked, burned or planted for the camera, and no tree is taken out of sequence to make a shot. The crew are filmed as people doing skilled, hot, dangerous work, never as illustrations of anything, and nothing in the film comments on anyone's livelihood. The film is not an argument for or against plantation forestry and does not present one block as evidence about a national policy. It contains no dying person, no patient, no bereaved family, no funeral and no death of any kind, and it never suggests that a tree, a block or a plantation has a mind.
position_hint: late in the group: it is the group's clearest statement of continuity without a traveller, so it works best once the earlier films have established that the series describes mechanisms rather than pronouncing on people, and it hands on to whatever closes the group. No location reasoning is involved.
risks: Letting the plantation be heard as having a mind, a life-continuum or a rebirth, when the sources are describing minds and the film must say so.
Letting 'nothing passes over' collapse into 'it lives on in the next stand', which is precisely the reading the C061 digest names as a distortion.

Being taken for an argument about forestry policy. Clear-felling of state plantations in Sri Lanka is politically contested and the film has no position in that argument; a single licensed rotation must not be edited into evidence for or against anything.
Aestheticising a felling so that the work looks like destruction, or so that it looks like nothing.
Letting 'the order of felling' be heard as a ranking of the trees, or the sources' order be heard as a ranking of people.
Any implication that a last thought can be arranged, or that a calm or a hard death shows anything about anyone.
Filming close to a felling in a way that endangers a crew or slows their work.
drop_if: No block is actually due for felling and replanting inside the production window, so the film's join cannot be filmed at all.
Permission from the forest authority, the licensee and the crew cannot be had, or filming would slow or endanger the work.
The only available operation is contested, unlicensed or under investigation, so that the film could not avoid becoming an argument about forestry.
The felling and the planting fall in different years, so the two halves of the film cannot be held together honestly.

connections.note: The same question about order, asked at a gate and at an extraction road: what goes first is decided by what is reachable, not by what is best.
Two cohorts set going long ago and coming due now: one palm that chooses its own year, one block whose year was chosen for it.
Two films on the near-death process without anybody dying: one on something that cannot be kept overnight, one on something that cannot be kept past a rotation.
A film that says nothing goes across the join hands on naturally to a practice of sitting with the fact of an ending.

selection.reason: It carries the group's central claim, continuity with no traveller, on a place where both ends of the join are dated and neither shares any material with the other, and it does it with nobody dying.

review.note: Rewritten 2026-09-23 into the footage-led shape. What was dropped: the entire old subject, in which a monk was followed into house after house where somebody was close to death, with the family's rearranged room, the chanting at the door and the hours in the house. It filmed dying people who cannot consent and families who cannot meaningfully refuse a camera, and the C062 digest's own limit, that no observer can see what arises in a dying mind, meant the film could never show the thing it was about. The old file's alternative strand, a night nurse sitting with patients whose families cannot be there, was dropped for the same reason, and with it the absorbed hospital-ward idea. The two merges the old file recorded are undone: IDEA-0135 stands on its own again, and this file no longer lists it as absorbed. All three concepts were kept and rebuilt from the digests on a location where an ending is attended as ordinary work: an even-aged planted stand reaching the end of its rotation and the same ground being planted again. C061's near-death and deathbed material, and the expert check the digest asks for before any film treats deathbed practices, are now simply out of scope, because the film has no deathbed in it. Every citation was checked against digest evidence rather than carried over from the old text.

suggested_location.name: A mature dry-zone hardwood plantation block in the forest country north-east of Kahatagasdigiliya, toward Horowpothana

also_known_as.name: thekka
also_known_as.meaning: teak, the species most of the dry-zone state plantations are planted with

also_known_as.name: the coupe
also_known_as.meaning: the block scheduled for felling in a given season

suggested_location.region: Anuradhapura District, North Central Province: the flat dry-zone forest, tank and paddy country in the north-east of the district, between Kahatagasdigiliya and Horowpothana, away from the city and the ancient sites
suggested_location.why_here: Because the dry zone is where Sri Lanka's planted hardwood is, and because a plantation block is the only thing in the landscape that is a cohort. Teak planting in the dry zone expanded in the nineteen-sixties and seventies on degraded natural forest, and most of the mature plantation standing in the country today comes from that period; the Forest Department manages tens of thousands of hectares of inventoried teak plantation, most of it in the dry zone, with Anuradhapura among the divisions that hold it, and dry-zone teak is worked on a rotation of about two decades, with even-aged mature blocks released for clear-felling and enumerated block by block. That is exactly the object the film needs: a stand whose start date and end date are both on record, whose ending arrives for every tree at once, and whose ground is planted again in the following rains. This part of the district is chosen deliberately away from the city and the monastic sites, so that the film is about a planted block in ordinary working country and not about antiquity.
what_to_film: The whole mosaic from directly overhead at several heights, so that a cut block, a young block, a closing block and a mature block read together as one rotation laid out side by side.
The standing block from inside at both ends of the day, with low sun going down the planting lines.
The marking crew and the felling as ordinary work: the paint mark, the saw, the fall, the limbing, the number written on a cut end, the extraction.
The last standing tree of a block, alone among stumps, in flat light and without dramatising it.
One stump from directly above, close enough that the rings are legible as a record of wide and narrow years.
The cut block as a whole, from height, with the stumps in ranks throwing shadows.
The first rains on the same ground, and the planting going in between the old stumps.
The young stand a year on, with the grey stumps still in it, and the next mature block beyond it, untouched.
suggested_location.access: By road from the trunk highways that cross this part of the district. Everything depends on the Forest Department division, on whoever holds the felling licence and on the crew, and a felling site is an active industrial workplace with real danger, so access is on their safety terms or not at all. The film needs two visits in one year, the felling and the planting, which means agreement well ahead of the season. Drone flight over a state forest plantation is likely to need specific permission from the department as well as whatever the aviation rules require.
suggested_location.best_time: The dry-season felling window, whenever the division's schedule puts it, for the hard light, the dust and the work; and the first weeks of the following rains for the planting. Within a day, the first and last hour, when shadows make the planting geometry unmistakable from height.

suggested_location.research_note: That dry-zone teak planting in Sri Lanka expanded in the nineteen-sixties and seventies on degraded natural forest, that most of the mature teak plantation standing today comes from that period, that the Forest Department manages on the order of twenty-eight thousand hectares of inventoried teak plantation with the majority in the dry zone, that dry-zone teak is assumed to run on a rotation of about twenty-one years, that even-aged mature plantations are selected for clear-felling, and that plantations released to the State Timber Corporation are fully enumerated block by block, is all from the sources above and is desk research only. That Anuradhapura is one of the dry-zone forest divisions holding teak plantation is from the same desk research. No block has been identified, no felling schedule has been seen, and nobody at the department, the corporation or any crew has been approached. The coordinates are a point in the dry-zone forest country of the north-east of the district, not a surveyed block. Whether a block in this area is due in any given season, and whether a felling and the following planting can both be filmed in one year, are the film's central unknowns. Clear-felling of state plantations is a contested subject in Sri Lanka and the location must be chosen so that the film is not standing inside a live dispute. Both images are of teak plantations in India and neither shows this location.

unknowns: Whether a block in this district is scheduled for clear-felling and replanting inside the production window. Nothing has been identified and this is the question that decides whether the film exists.
Whether the Forest Department, the licensee and the crew would allow filming on an active felling site, and on what safety terms.
Whether a drone can be flown over a state forest plantation here at all.
Whether the felling and the following planting reliably fall inside one year at this location, which the film's second half depends on.

The C056 digest asks for an expert check on the compressed line that carries the pen-and-gate simile; the film's fourth beat is written so that it does not depend on either reading, but the check should happen before the cut.
Whether a plantation operation can be filmed in Sri Lanka at present without the film being read as taking a side in the public argument about plantation clear-felling.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. The location is proposed by Claude from desk research and is unverified. No scene or shot is decided here.
